content.latin: Quóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu eius sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
content.english: For the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.

content.latin: Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius (genuflectitur) veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.
content.english: For the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. (genuflect) Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.

content.latin: Hódie, si vocem eius audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
content.english: Today if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.

content.latin: Quadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus iurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
content.english: Forty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.

segments.t: Psalmus 23

content.latin: 23:1 Dómini est terra, et plenitúdo eius: * orbis terrárum, et univérsi qui hábitant in eo.
content.english: 23:1 The earth is the Lord’s and the fulness thereof: * the world, and all they that dwell therein.

segments.t: Dómini est terra, et plenitúdo eius: * orbis terrárum, et univérsi qui hábitant in eo.

content.latin: 23:2 Quia ipse super mária fundávit eum: * et super flúmina præparávit eum.
content.english: 23:2 For he hath founded it upon the seas; * and hath prepared it upon the rivers.

segments.t: Quia ipse super mária fundávit eum: * et super flúmina præparávit eum.

content.latin: 23:3 Quis ascéndet in montem Dómini? * aut quis stabit in loco sancto eius?
content.english: 23:3 Who shall ascend into the mountain of the Lord: * or who shall stand in his holy place?

segments.t: Quis ascéndet in montem Dómini? * aut quis stabit in loco sancto eius?

content.latin: 23:4 Ínnocens mánibus et mundo corde, * qui non accépit in vano ánimam suam, nec iurávit in dolo próximo suo.
content.english: 23:4 The innocent in hands, and clean of heart, * who hath not taken his soul in vain, nor sworn deceitfully to his neighbour.

segments.t: Ínnocens mánibus et mundo corde, * qui non accépit in vano ánimam suam, nec iurávit in dolo próximo suo.

content.latin: 23:5 Hic accípiet benedictiónem a Dómino: * et misericórdiam a Deo, salutári suo.
content.english: 23:5 He shall receive a blessing from the Lord, * and mercy from God his Saviour.

segments.t: Hic accípiet benedictiónem a Dómino: * et misericórdiam a Deo, salutári suo.

content.latin: 23:6 Hæc est generátio quæréntium eum, * quæréntium fáciem Dei Iacob.
content.english: 23:6 This is the generation of them that seek him, * of them that seek the face of the God of Jacob.

segments.t: Hæc est generátio quæréntium eum, * quæréntium fáciem Dei Iacob.

content.latin: 23:7 Attóllite portas, príncipes, vestras, et elevámini, portæ æternáles: * et introíbit Rex glóriæ.
content.english: 23:7 Lift up your gates, O ye princes, and be ye lifted up, O eternal gates: * and the King of Glory shall enter in.

segments.t: Attóllite portas, príncipes, vestras, et elevámini, portæ æternáles: * et introíbit Rex glóriæ.

content.latin: 23:8 Quis est iste Rex glóriæ? * Dóminus fortis et potens: Dóminus potens in prǽlio.
content.english: 23:8 Who is this King of Glory? * the Lord who is strong and mighty: the Lord mighty in battle.

segments.t: Quis est iste Rex glóriæ? * Dóminus fortis et potens: Dóminus potens in prǽlio.

segments.t: Attóllite portas, príncipes, vestras, et elevámini, portæ æternáles: * et introíbit Rex glóriæ.

content.latin: 23:10 Quis est iste Rex glóriæ? * Dóminus virtútum ipse est Rex glóriæ.

segments.t: Quis est iste Rex glóriæ? * Dóminus virtútum ipse est Rex glóriæ.

segments.t: Psalmus 45

content.latin: 45:2 Deus noster refúgium, et virtus: * adiútor in tribulatiónibus, quæ invenérunt nos nimis.
content.english: 45:2 Our God is our refuge and strength: * a helper in troubles, which have found us exceedingly.

segments.t: Deus noster refúgium, et virtus: * adiútor in tribulatiónibus, quæ invenérunt nos nimis.

content.latin: 45:3 Proptérea non timébimus dum turbábitur terra: * et transferéntur montes in cor maris.
content.english: 45:3 Therefore we will not fear, when the earth shall be troubled; * and the mountains shall be removed into the heart of the sea.

segments.t: Proptérea non timébimus dum turbábitur terra: * et transferéntur montes in cor maris.

content.latin: 45:4 Sonuérunt, et turbátæ sunt aquæ eórum: * conturbáti sunt montes in fortitúdine eius.
content.english: 45:4 Their waters roared and were troubled: * the mountains were troubled with his strength.

segments.t: Sonuérunt, et turbátæ sunt aquæ eórum: * conturbáti sunt montes in fortitúdine eius.

content.latin: 45:5 Flúminis ímpetus lætíficat civitátem Dei: * sanctificávit tabernáculum suum Altíssimus.
content.english: 45:5 The stream of the river maketh the city of God joyful: * the most High hath sanctified his own tabernacle.

segments.t: Flúminis ímpetus lætíficat civitátem Dei: * sanctificávit tabernáculum suum Altíssimus.

content.latin: 45:6 Deus in médio eius, non commovébitur: * adiuvábit eam Deus mane dilúculo.
content.english: 45:6 God is in the midst thereof, it shall not be moved: * God will help it in the morning early.

segments.t: Deus in médio eius, non commovébitur: * adiuvábit eam Deus mane dilúculo.

content.latin: 45:7 Conturbátæ sunt gentes, et inclináta sunt regna: * dedit vocem suam, mota est terra.
content.english: 45:7 Nations were troubled, and kingdoms were bowed down: * he uttered his voice, the earth trembled.

segments.t: Conturbátæ sunt gentes, et inclináta sunt regna: * dedit vocem suam, mota est terra.

content.latin: 45:8 Dóminus virtútum nobíscum: * suscéptor noster Deus Iacob.
content.english: 45:8 The Lord of armies is with us: * the God of Jacob is our protector.

segments.t: Dóminus virtútum nobíscum: * suscéptor noster Deus Iacob.

content.latin: 45:9 Veníte, et vidéte ópera Dómini, quæ pósuit prodígia super terram: * áuferens bella usque ad finem terræ.
content.english: 45:9 Come and behold ye the works of the Lord: what wonders he hath done upon earth, * making wars to cease even to the end of the earth.

segments.t: Veníte, et vidéte ópera Dómini, quæ pósuit prodígia super terram: * áuferens bella usque ad finem terræ.

content.latin: 45:10 Arcum cónteret, et confrínget arma: * et scuta combúret igni.
content.english: 45:10 He shall destroy the bow, and break the weapons: * and the shield he shall burn in the fire.

segments.t: Arcum cónteret, et confrínget arma: * et scuta combúret igni.

content.latin: 45:11 Vacáte, et vidéte quóniam ego sum Deus: * exaltábor in géntibus, et exaltábor in terra.
content.english: 45:11 Be still and see that I am God; * I will be exalted among the nations, and I will be exalted in the earth.

segments.t: Vacáte, et vidéte quóniam ego sum Deus: * exaltábor in géntibus, et exaltábor in terra.

content.latin: Psalmus 47 [3]
content.english: Psalm 47 [3]

segments.t: Psalmus 47

content.latin: 47:2 Magnus Dóminus, et laudábilis nimis * in civitáte Dei nostri, in monte sancto eius.
content.english: 47:2 Great is the Lord, and exceedingly to be praised * in the city of our God, in his holy mountain.

segments.t: Magnus Dóminus, et laudábilis nimis * in civitáte Dei nostri, in monte sancto eius.

content.latin: 47:3 Fundátur exsultatióne univérsæ terræ mons Sion, * látera Aquilónis, cívitas Regis magni.
content.english: 47:3 With the joy of the whole earth is mount Sion founded, * on the sides of the north, the city of the great king.

segments.t: Fundátur exsultatióne univérsæ terræ mons Sion, * látera Aquilónis, cívitas Regis magni.

content.latin: 47:4 Deus in dómibus eius cognoscétur: * cum suscípiet eam.
content.english: 47:4 In her houses shall God be known, * when he shall protect her.

segments.t: Deus in dómibus eius cognoscétur: * cum suscípiet eam.

content.latin: 47:5 Quóniam ecce reges terræ congregáti sunt: * convenérunt in unum.
content.english: 47:5 For behold the kings of the earth assembled themselves: * they gathered together.

segments.t: Quóniam ecce reges terræ congregáti sunt: * convenérunt in unum.

content.latin: 47:6 Ipsi vidéntes sic admiráti sunt, conturbáti sunt, commóti sunt: * tremor apprehéndit eos.
content.english: 47:6 So they saw, and they wondered, they were troubled, they were moved: * trembling took hold of them.

segments.t: Ipsi vidéntes sic admiráti sunt, conturbáti sunt, commóti sunt: * tremor apprehéndit eos.

content.latin: 47:7 Ibi dolóres ut parturiéntis: * in spíritu veheménti cónteres naves Tharsis.
content.english: 47:7 There were pains as of a woman in labour; * with a vehement wind thou shalt break in pieces the ships of Tharsis.

segments.t: Ibi dolóres ut parturiéntis: * in spíritu veheménti cónteres naves Tharsis.

content.latin: 47:9 Sicut audívimus, sic vídimus in civitáte Dómini virtútum, in civitáte Dei nostri: * Deus fundávit eam in ætérnum.
content.english: 47:9 As we have heard, so have we seen, in the city of the Lord of hosts, in the city of our God: * God hath founded it for ever.

segments.t: Sicut audívimus, sic vídimus in civitáte Dómini virtútum, in civitáte Dei nostri: * Deus fundávit eam in ætérnum.

content.latin: 47:10 Suscépimus, Deus, misericórdiam tuam, * in médio templi tui.
content.english: 47:10 We have received thy mercy, O God, * in the midst of thy temple.

segments.t: Suscépimus, Deus, misericórdiam tuam, * in médio templi tui.

content.latin: 47:11 Secúndum nomen tuum, Deus, sic et laus tua in fines terræ: * iustítia plena est déxtera tua.
content.english: 47:11 According to thy name, O God, so also is thy praise unto the ends of the earth: * thy right hand is full of justice.

segments.t: Secúndum nomen tuum, Deus, sic et laus tua in fines terræ: * iustítia plena est déxtera tua.

content.latin: 47:12 Lætétur mons Sion, et exsúltent fíliæ Iudæ: * propter iudícia tua, Dómine.
content.english: 47:12 Let mount Sion rejoice, and the daughters of Juda be glad; * because of thy judgments, O Lord.

segments.t: Lætétur mons Sion, et exsúltent fíliæ Iudæ: * propter iudícia tua, Dómine.

content.latin: 47:13 Circúmdate Sion, et complectímini eam: * narráte in túrribus eius.
content.english: 47:13 Surround Sion, and encompass her: * tell ye in her towers.

segments.t: Circúmdate Sion, et complectímini eam: * narráte in túrribus eius.

content.latin: 47:14 Pónite corda vestra in virtúte eius: * et distribúite domos eius, ut enarrétis in progénie áltera.

content.latin: 83:2 Quam dilécta tabernácula tua, Dómine virtútum: * concupíscit, et déficit ánima mea in átria Dómini.
content.english: 83:2 How lovely are thy tabernacles, O Lord of hosts! * my soul longeth and fainteth for the courts of the Lord.

segments.t: Quam dilécta tabernácula tua, Dómine virtútum: * concupíscit, et déficit ánima mea in átria Dómini.

content.latin: 83:3 Cor meum, et caro mea * exsultavérunt in Deum vivum.
content.english: 83:3 My heart and my flesh * have rejoiced in the living God.

segments.t: Cor meum, et caro mea * exsultavérunt in Deum vivum.

content.latin: 83:4 Étenim passer invénit sibi domum: * et turtur nidum sibi, ubi ponat pullos suos.
content.english: 83:4 For the sparrow hath found herself a house, * and the turtledove a nest for herself where she may lay her young ones:

segments.t: Étenim passer invénit sibi domum: * et turtur nidum sibi, ubi ponat pullos suos.

content.latin: 83:4 Altária tua, Dómine virtútum: * Rex meus, et Deus meus.
content.english: 83:4 Thy altars, O Lord of hosts, * my king and my God.

segments.t: Altária tua, Dómine virtútum: * Rex meus, et Deus meus.

content.latin: 83:5 Beáti, qui hábitant in domo tua, Dómine: * in sǽcula sæculórum laudábunt te.
content.english: 83:5 Blessed are they that dwell in thy house, O Lord: * they shall praise thee for ever and ever.

segments.t: Beáti, qui hábitant in domo tua, Dómine: * in sǽcula sæculórum laudábunt te.

content.english: 83:6 Blessed is the man whose help is from thee: * in his heart he hath disposed to ascend by steps, in the vale of tears, in the place which he hath set.

segments.t: Beátus vir, cuius est auxílium abs te: * ascensiónes in corde suo dispósuit, in valle lacrimárum in loco, quem pósuit.

segments.t: Étenim benedictiónem dabit legislátor, ibunt de virtúte in virtútem: * vidébitur Deus deórum in Sion.

segments.t: Dómine, Deus virtútum, exáudi oratiónem meam: * áuribus pércipe, Deus Iacob.

content.latin: 83:10 Protéctor noster, áspice, Deus: * et réspice in fáciem Christi tui:
content.english: 83:10 Behold, O God our protector: * and look on the face of thy Christ.

segments.t: Protéctor noster, áspice, Deus: * et réspice in fáciem Christi tui:

content.latin: 83:11 Quia mélior est dies una in átriis tuis, * super míllia.
content.english: 83:11 For better is one day in thy courts * above thousands.

segments.t: Quia mélior est dies una in átriis tuis, * super míllia.

content.latin: 83:11 Elégi abiéctus esse in domo Dei mei: * magis quam habitáre in tabernáculis peccatórum.
content.english: 83:11 I have chosen to be an abject in the house of my God, * rather than to dwell in the tabernacles of sinners.

segments.t: Elégi abiéctus esse in domo Dei mei: * magis quam habitáre in tabernáculis peccatórum.

segments.t: Quia misericórdiam, et veritátem díligit Deus: * grátiam et glóriam dabit Dóminus.

content.latin: Sed, ubi Constantínus imperátor per baptísmi sacraméntum sanitátem salutémque consecútus est, tum primum lege ab eo lata concéssum est toto orbe terrárum, Christiáni ut ecclésias ædificárent; quos ille, non solum edícto, sed étiam exémplo ad sacram ædificatiónem est cohortátus. Nam, et in suo Lateranénsi palátio ecclésiam Salvatóri dedicávit, et ei continéntem basílicam nómine sancti Ioánnis Baptístæ cóndidit, eo loco quo ipse, baptizátus a sancto Silvéstro, ab infidelitátis lepra mundátus est; quam idem Póntifex consecrávit quinto idus novémbris. Cuius consecratiónis memória celebrátur hodiérno die, quo primum Romæ públice ecclésia consecráta est, et imágo Salvatóris, in paríete depícta, pópulo Románo appáruit.
content.english: But when the Emperor Constantine had by the Sacrament of Baptism received health both of body and soul, then first in a law by him published was it allowed to the Christians throughout the whole world to build Churches, to the which holy building he exhorted them by his example as well as by his decree. He dedicated in his own Lateran Palace a Church to the Saviour, and built hard by it a Cathedral in the name of St. John the Baptist, upon the place where he had been baptized by holy Sylvester and cleansed from his leprosy. This Cathedral was hallowed by the said Pope upon the 9th day of November. It is this consecration, the memory whereof is still celebrated upon this day, the first whereon the public consecration of a Church ever took place in Rome, and the image of the Saviour was seen by the Roman people painted upon the wall.

content.latin: Quod, si beátus Silvéster póstea in consecratióne altáris Príncipis Apostolórum decrévit ut deínceps nisi ex lápide altária non ædificaréntur; tamen basílicæ Lateranénsis altáre fuit e ligno eréctum. Quod mirum non est; nam, cum a sancto Petro usque ad Silvéstrum, propter persecutiónes, Pontífices certo loco consístere non possent, quocúmque eos necéssitas compulísset, sive in cryptas, sive in cœmetéria, sive in ædes piórum, super illo altári lígneo ad arcæ similitúdinem cóncavo, sacra faciébant. Quo altári sanctus Silvéster, réddita Ecclésiæ pace, honóris causa Príncipis Apostolórum, qui in illo sacrificásse dícitur, et reliquórum Pontíficum, qui usque ad id tempus ad mystéria conficiénda eo usi fúerant, in Lateranénsi prima ecclésia collocáto, sancívit ne quisquam in eo, præter Románum Pontíficem, Missam deínceps celebráret.
content.english: The Blessed Sylvester afterwards decreed, when he was consecrating the Altar of the Prince of the Apostles, that Altars were thenceforward to be made of stone only, but notwithstanding this the Lateran Cathedral hath the altar made of wood. This is not surprising. From St. Peter to Sylvester the Popes had not been able, by reason of persecutions, to abide fixedly in one place, and they celebrated the Holy Liturgy in cellars, in burying-places, in the houses of godly persons, or wherever need drove them, upon a wooden altar made like an empty box. When peace was given to the Church, holy Sylvester took this box, and to do honour to the Prince of the Apostles, who is said to have offered sacrifice thereon, and to the other Popes who thereon had been used to execute the mystery even unto that time, set it in the first Church, even the Lateran, and ordained that no one but the Bishop of Rome should celebrate the Liturgy thereon for all time coming. s/$/~/

content.latin: Eándem ecclésiam incéndiis, vastatiónibus, terræ ínsuper mótibus disiéctam eversámque, ac sédula summórum Pontíficum cura reparátam, nova póstmodum molitióne restitútam, Benedíctus décimus tértius, Póntifex máximus, órdinis Prædicatórum, die vigésima octáva aprílis anni millésimi septingentésimi vigésimi sexti, ritu solémni consecrávit, eiúsque celebritátis memóriam hac die recoléndam státuit. Quod autem Pius nonus perficiéndum censúerat, Leo décimus tértius cellam máximam, vetustáte fatiscéntem, ingénti molitióne producéndam laxandámque curávit; vetus musívum, multis iam ántea pártibus instaurátum, ad antíquum exémplar restítui et in novam ábsidem, ópere cultúque magnífico exornátam, transférri; aulam transvérsam, laqueári et contignatióne reféctis, expolíri iussit, anno millésimo octingentésimo octuagésimo quarto; sacrário, æde canonicórum, perpetuáque ad baptistérium Constantiniánum pórticu adiéctis.
content.english: The original Lateran Cathedral, cast down and destroyed by fires, pillage, and earthquakes, and renewed by the constant care of the Popes, was at last rebuilt afresh, and solemnly consecrated by Pope Benedict XIII, a Friar Preacher, upon the 28th day of April, in the year 1726, the memory of which Festival he ordained to be kept upon this day. In the year 1884 Leo XIII took in hand a work which had received the sanction of his predecessor Pius IX. The great sanctuary, the walls of which were giving way with age, was lengthened and widened, a task of immense labour. The ancient mosaic had been renewed previously in several places; it was now restored according to the original design, and transferred to the new apse, the embellishment of which was carried out with great magnificence. The transept was redecorated, and its ceiling and woodwork repaired. A sacristy, a residence for the canons, and a portico connecting with the baptistery of Constantine, were added to the existing buildings.

segments.t: Lib. 8 in Luc., prope finem

content.latin: Zachǽus, statúra pusíllus, hoc est, nulla nobilitátis ingénitæ dignitáte sublímis, exíguus méritis sicut pópulus natiónum, audíto Dómini Salvatóris advéntu, quem sui non recéperant, vidére cupiébat. Sed nemo fácile Iesum videt; nemo potest Iesum vidére constitútus in terra. Et, quia non prophétas, non legem habébat, tamquam formæ grátiam naturális, ascéndit in sycómorum, vanitátem scílicet Iudæórum vestígio suo próterens, erráta quoque córrigens superióris ætátis. Et ídeo Iesum in interióris domus recépit hospítio.
content.english: Zacchaeus was little of stature, that is, he was not raised aloft among men by nobility of birth, and, like the most of the world, he possessed few merits. When he heard that the Lord and Saviour, Who had come unto His Own, and Whom His Own had not received, John i. 11, was coming, he desired to see Him. But the sight of Jesus is not easy; to any on the earth it is impossible. And since Zacchaeus had neither the Prophets, nor yet the Law, as a gracious help to his nature, he climbed up into a sycamore tree, raising his feet above the vanity of the Jews, and straightening the crooked branches of his former life, and therefore he received Jesus to lodge within his house.

content.latin: Et bene ascéndit in árborem, ut arbor bona bonos fructus fáceret, ac, naturáli excísus oleástro et contra natúram insértus in bonam olívam, fructum posset legis afférre. Radix enim sancta, etsi rami inútiles. Quorum infructuósam glóriam plebs géntium, fide resurrectiónis, quasi quadam córporis elevatióne, transcéndit. Zachǽus ergo in sycómoro, cæcus in via: quorum álterum Dóminus miseratúrus exspéctat, álterum mansiónis suæ claritáte nobílitat; álterum sanatúrus intérrogat, apud álterum se, non invitátus, invítat. Sciébat enim úberem hospítii sui esse mercédem. Sed tamen, etsi nondum vocem invitántis audíerat, iam víderat afféctum.
content.english: He did well to climb up into a tree, that a good tree might bring forth good fruits, Matth. vii. 17, and that the slip of the wild olive, grafted, contrary to nature, into the good olive, might bring forth the fruits of the law. Rom. xi. 17, 24. For the root is holy, however unprofitable the branches. Their barren beauty hath now been overshadowed by the belief of the Gentiles in the Resurrection, as by a material upgrowth. Zacchaeus, then, was in the sycamore tree, and the blind man by the way-side, xviii. 35. For the one, Jesus stood waiting to show mercy, and asked him before He healed him, what he would that He should do for him; being unbidden of the other, He bade Himself to be his Guest, knowing how rich was the reward of receiving Him. Nevertheless, albeit He had heard no words of invitation, yet had He seen how his heart went.

content.latin: Verum, ne cæcum illum, tamquam fastidiósi páuperum, cito reliquísse videámur et transísse ad dívitem, exspectémus eum, quia exspectávit et Dóminus; interrogémus eum, quia interrogávit et Christus. Nos interrogémus, quia nescímus: ille, quia nóverat. Nos interrogémus, ut sciámus unde iste curátus sit: ille interrogávit, ut in uno plures discerémus unde Dóminum vidére mereámur. Interrogávit enim, ut crederémus, néminem, nisi confiténtem, posse salvári.
content.english: But lest we should seem haughtily to pass by the poor blind man, and to hurry on to the rich one, let us stand waiting for him, as the Lord stood and waited; let us ask of him, as Christ asked of him. Let us ask, because we are ignorant; Christ asked, because He knew. Let us ask, that we may know whence he received his cure; Christ asked, that all of us may know from one example where through we are to earn a sight of the Lord. Christ asked, that we might believe that none, save they that confess Him, can be saved.

content.latin: 148:1 Laudáte Dóminum de cælis: * laudáte eum in excélsis.
content.english: 148:1 Praise ye the Lord from the heavens * praise ye him in the high places.

segments.t: Laudáte Dóminum de cælis: * laudáte eum in excélsis.

content.latin: 148:2 Laudáte eum, omnes Ángeli eius: * laudáte eum, omnes virtútes eius.
content.english: 148:2 Praise ye him, all his angels: * praise ye him, all his hosts.

segments.t: Laudáte eum, omnes Ángeli eius: * laudáte eum, omnes virtútes eius.

content.latin: 148:3 Laudáte eum, sol et luna: * laudáte eum, omnes stellæ et lumen.
content.english: 148:3 Praise ye him, O sun and moon: * praise him, all ye stars and light.

segments.t: Laudáte eum, sol et luna: * laudáte eum, omnes stellæ et lumen.

content.latin: 148:4 Laudáte eum, cæli cælórum: * et aquæ omnes, quæ super cælos sunt, laudent nomen Dómini.
content.english: 148:4 Praise him, ye heavens of heavens: * and let all the waters that are above the heavens, praise the name of the Lord.

segments.t: Laudáte eum, cæli cælórum: * et aquæ omnes, quæ super cælos sunt, laudent nomen Dómini.

content.latin: 148:5 Quia ipse dixit, et facta sunt: * ipse mandávit, et creáta sunt.
content.english: 148:5 For he spoke, and they were made: * he commanded, and they were created.

segments.t: Quia ipse dixit, et facta sunt: * ipse mandávit, et creáta sunt.

content.latin: 148:6 Státuit ea in ætérnum, et in sǽculum sǽculi: * præcéptum pósuit, et non præteríbit.
content.english: 148:6 He hath established them for ever, and for ages of ages: * he hath made a decree, and it shall not pass away.

segments.t: Státuit ea in ætérnum, et in sǽculum sǽculi: * præcéptum pósuit, et non præteríbit.

content.latin: 148:7 Laudáte Dóminum de terra, * dracónes, et omnes abýssi.
content.english: 148:7 Praise the Lord from the earth, * ye dragons, and all ye deeps:

segments.t: Laudáte Dóminum de terra, * dracónes, et omnes abýssi.

content.latin: 148:8 Ignis, grando, nix, glácies, spíritus procellárum: * quæ fáciunt verbum eius:
content.english: 148:8 Fire, hail, snow, ice, stormy winds * which fulfill his word:

segments.t: Ignis, grando, nix, glácies, spíritus procellárum: * quæ fáciunt verbum eius:

content.latin: 148:9 Montes, et omnes colles: * ligna fructífera, et omnes cedri.
content.english: 148:9 Mountains and all hills, * fruitful trees and all cedars:

segments.t: Montes, et omnes colles: * ligna fructífera, et omnes cedri.

content.latin: 148:10 Béstiæ, et univérsa pécora: * serpéntes, et vólucres pennátæ:
content.english: 148:10 Beasts and all cattle: * serpents and feathered fowls:

segments.t: Béstiæ, et univérsa pécora: * serpéntes, et vólucres pennátæ:

content.english: 148:11 Kings of the earth and all people: * princes and all judges of the earth:

segments.t: Reges terræ, et omnes pópuli: * príncipes, et omnes iúdices terræ.

content.english: 148:12 Young men and maidens: let the old with the younger, praise the name of the Lord: * For his name alone is exalted.

segments.t: Iúvenes, et vírgines: senes cum iunióribus laudent nomen Dómini: * quia exaltátum est nomen eius solíus.

content.latin: Hymnus
content.english: Hymn

segments.t: Hymnus

content.latin: Alto ex Olýmpi vértice
content.english: From highest heaven, the Father's Son,

content.latin: Summi Paréntis Fílius,
content.english: Descending like that mystic stone

content.latin: Ceu monte deséctus lapis
content.english: Cut from a mountain without hands,

content.latin: Terras in imas décidens,
content.english: Came down below, and filled all lands;

content.latin: Domus supérnæ et ínfimæ
content.english: Uniting, midway in the sky,

content.latin: Utrúmque iunxit ángulum.
content.english: His house on earth, and house on high.

content.latin: Sed illa sedes cǽlitum
content.english: That house on high,  it ever rings

content.latin: Semper resúltat láudibus,
content.english: With praises of the King of kings;

content.latin: Deúmque trinum et únicum
content.english: Forever there, on harps divine,

content.latin: Iugi canóre prǽdicat:
content.english: They hymn th' eternal One and Trine;

content.latin: Illi canéntes iúngimur
content.english: We, here below, the strain prolong,

content.latin: Almæ Siónis ǽmuli.
content.english: And faintly echo Sion's song.

content.latin: Hæc templa, Rex cæléstium,
content.english: O Lord of lords invisible!

content.latin: Imple benígno lúmine:
content.english: With thy pure light this temple fill:

content.latin: Huc, o rogátus, ádveni,
content.english: Hither, oft as invoked, descend;

content.latin: Plebísque vota súscipe,
content.english: Here to thy people's prayer attend;

content.latin: Et nostra corda iúgiter
content.english: Here, through all hearts, forevermore,

content.latin: Perfúnde cæli grátia.
content.english: thy Spirit's quick'ning graces pour.

content.latin: Hic ímpetrent fidélium
content.english: Here may the faithful, day by day,

content.latin: Voces precésque súpplicum
content.english: Their hearts' adoring homage pay;

content.latin: Domus beátæ múnera,
content.english: And here receive from thy dear love

content.latin: Partísque donis gáudeant:
content.english: The blessings of that home above;

content.latin: Donec, solúti córpore,
content.english: Till loosened from this mortal chain,

content.latin: Sedes beátas ímpleant.
content.english: Its everlasting joys they gain.

content.latin: Decus Parénti débitum
content.english: To God the Father, glory due

content.latin: Sit usquequáque Altíssimo,
content.english: Be paid by all the heavenly host;

content.latin: Natóque Patris único,
content.english: And to his only Son most true;

content.latin: Et ínclito Paráclito,
content.english: With thee, O mighty Holy Ghost!

content.latin: Cui laus, potéstas, glória
content.english: To whom, praise, power, and blessing be,

content.latin: Ætérna sit per sǽcula.
content.english: Through th' ages of eternity,

content.latin: Amen.
content.english: Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Hæc est domus Dómini fírmiter ædificáta.
content.english: ℣. This is the house of God, stoutly builded.

segments.t: Hæc est domus Dómini fírmiter ædificáta.

content.latin: ℟. Bene fundáta est supra firmam petram.

content.latin: Ant. Zachǽe, * festínans descénde, quia hódie in domo tua opórtet me manére. At ille festínans descéndit, et suscépit illum gaudens in domum suam. Hódie huic dómui salus a Deo facta est, allelúia.
content.english: Ant. Zacchaeus, make haste and come down, for today I must abide at thy house. * And he made haste and came down, and received Him joyfully into his house. This day is salvation come from God to this house. Alleluia.

content.latin: 1:68 Benedíctus ✠ Dóminus, Deus Israël: * quia visitávit, et fecit redemptiónem plebis suæ:
content.english: 1:68 Blessed be the Lord ✠ God of Israel; * because he hath visited and wrought the redemption of his people:

segments.t: Benedíctus ✠ Dóminus, Deus Israël: * quia visitávit, et fecit redemptiónem plebis suæ:

content.latin: 1:69 Et eréxit cornu salútis nobis: * in domo David, púeri sui.
content.english: 1:69 And hath raised up an horn of salvation to us, * in the house of David his servant:

segments.t: Et eréxit cornu salútis nobis: * in domo David, púeri sui.

content.latin: 1:70 Sicut locútus est per os sanctórum, * qui a sǽculo sunt, prophetárum eius:
content.english: 1:70 As he spoke by the mouth of his holy Prophets, * who are from the beginning:

segments.t: Sicut locútus est per os sanctórum, * qui a sǽculo sunt, prophetárum eius:

content.latin: 1:71 Salútem ex inimícis nostris, * et de manu ómnium, qui odérunt nos.
content.english: 1:71 Salvation from our enemies, * and from the hand of all that hate us:

segments.t: Salútem ex inimícis nostris, * et de manu ómnium, qui odérunt nos.

content.latin: 1:72 Ad faciéndam misericórdiam cum pátribus nostris: * et memorári testaménti sui sancti.
content.english: 1:72 To perform mercy to our fathers, * and to remember his holy testament,

segments.t: Ad faciéndam misericórdiam cum pátribus nostris: * et memorári testaménti sui sancti.

content.latin: 1:73 Iusiurándum, quod iurávit ad Ábraham patrem nostrum, * datúrum se nobis:
content.english: 1:73 The oath, which he swore to Abraham our father, * that he would grant to us,

segments.t: Iusiurándum, quod iurávit ad Ábraham patrem nostrum, * datúrum se nobis:

content.latin: 1:74 Ut sine timóre, de manu inimicórum nostrórum liberáti, * serviámus illi.
content.english: 1:74 That being delivered from the hand of our enemies, * we may serve him without fear,

segments.t: Ut sine timóre, de manu inimicórum nostrórum liberáti, * serviámus illi.

content.latin: 1:75 In sanctitáte, et iustítia coram ipso, * ómnibus diébus nostris.
content.english: 1:75 In holiness and justice before him, * all our days.

segments.t: In sanctitáte, et iustítia coram ipso, * ómnibus diébus nostris.

content.latin: 1:76 Et tu, puer, Prophéta Altíssimi vocáberis: * præíbis enim ante fáciem Dómini, paráre vias eius:
content.english: 1:76 And thou, child, shalt be called the prophet of the Highest: * for thou shalt go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways:

segments.t: Et tu, puer, Prophéta Altíssimi vocáberis: * præíbis enim ante fáciem Dómini, paráre vias eius:

content.latin: 1:77 Ad dandam sciéntiam salútis plebi eius: * in remissiónem peccatórum eórum:
content.english: 1:77 To give knowledge of salvation to his people, * unto the remission of their sins:

segments.t: Ad dandam sciéntiam salútis plebi eius: * in remissiónem peccatórum eórum:

content.latin: 1:78 Per víscera misericórdiæ Dei nostri: * in quibus visitávit nos, óriens ex alto:
content.english: 1:78 Through the bowels of the mercy of our God, * in which the Orient from on high hath visited us:

segments.t: Per víscera misericórdiæ Dei nostri: * in quibus visitávit nos, óriens ex alto:

content.latin: 1:79 Illumináre his, qui in ténebris, et in umbra mortis sedent: * ad dirigéndos pedes nostros in viam pacis.
content.english: 1:79 To enlighten them that sit in darkness, and in the shadow of death: * to direct our feet into the way of peace.

segments.t: Illumináre his, qui in ténebris, et in umbra mortis sedent: * ad dirigéndos pedes nostros in viam pacis.

content.latin: Deus, qui nobis per síngulos annos huius sancti templi tui consecratiónis réparas diem, et sacris semper mystériis repræséntas incólumes: exáudi preces pópuli tui, et præsta; ut quisquis hoc templum benefícia petitúrus ingréditur, cuncta se impetrásse lætétur.
content.english: O God, who dost every year bring round unto us again the day whereon this thine holy temple was hallowed, and bringest us again in soundness of body and mind to be present at thine holy worship, graciously hear the supplications of thy people, and grant that whosoever shall come into this thine house to ask good at thine hand, may be rejoiced in the obtaining of all his request.

content.latin: Romæ item natális sancti Leónis Papæ Primi, Confessóris et Ecclésiæ Doctóris; qui, virtútum excéllens méritis, dictus est Magnus. Tandem, cum sanxísset multa luculentérque scripsísset, Pastor bonus, de sancta Dei Ecclésia et univérso grege Domínico óptime méritus, quiévit in pace. Ipsíus tamen festívitas tértio Idus Aprílis celebrátur.
content.english: In the country of Agde, the holy martyrs Tiberius, Modestus, and Florence, who, in the time of the Emperor Diocletian, underwent diverse torments, and were crowned with martyrdom.

content.latin: Icónii, in Lycaónia, sanctárum mulíerum Tryphénnæ et Tryphósæ, quæ, beáti Pauli prædicatióne et exémplo Theclæ, in Christiána discíplina plúrimum profecérunt.
content.english: At Antioch, the holy martyrs Demetrius, Bishop (of that see,) the Deacon Anian, Eustosius, and twenty others.

content.latin: Antiochíæ sanctórum Demétrii Epíscopi, Aniáni Diáconi, Eustósii et aliórum vigínti Mártyrum.
content.english: At Ravenna, (in the year 142,) holy Probus, Bishop (of that see,) famous for miracles.

content.latin: In território Agathénsi, in Gállia, sanctórum Mártyrum Tibérii, Modésti et Floréntiæ; qui, témpore Diocletiáni, váriis torméntis cruciáti, martýrium complevérunt.
content.english: At Orleans, (in the fifth century,) the holy Confessor Monitor, Bishop (of that see.)

content.latin: Ravénnæ sancti Probi Epíscopi, miráculis clari.
content.english: In England, holy Justus, Bishop (of Rochester, afterwards translated to Canterbury,) who was sent into that island by the blessed Pope Gregory, along with Augustine, Mellitus, and others to preach the gospel, and there slept in the Lord, famous for holiness, (in the year 627.)

content.latin: Aureliánis, in Gállia, sancti Monitóris, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
content.english: At Melun is commemorated the holy Confessor Leo.

content.latin: In Anglia sancti Iusti Epíscopi, qui, una cum Augustíno, Mellíto et áliis a beáto Gregório Papa in eam ínsulam missus ad prædicándum Evangélium, ibídem, sanctitáte célebris, obdormívit in Dómino.
content.english: At Iconium, in Lycaonia, the holy Women Tryphenna and Tryphosa, who advanced much in Christian training by the preaching of blessed Paul and the example of Thecla.

content.latin: In óppido Milléduno, in Gállia, sancti Leónis Confessóris.

content.latin: Orémus.
content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: Dirígere et sanctificáre, régere et gubernáre dignáre, Dómine Deus, Rex cæli et terræ, hódie corda et córpora nostra, sensus, sermónes et actus nostros in lege tua, et in opéribus mandatórum tuórum: ut hic et in ætérnum, te auxiliánte, salvi et líberi esse mereámur, Salvátor mundi: Qui vivis et regnas in sǽcula sæculórum.

content.latin: 26:1 Dóminus illuminátio mea, et salus mea, * quem timébo?
content.english: 26:1 The Lord is my light and my salvation, * whom shall I fear?

segments.t: Dóminus illuminátio mea, et salus mea, * quem timébo?

content.latin: 26:1 Dóminus protéctor vitæ meæ, * a quo trepidábo?
content.english: 26:1 The Lord is the protector of my life: * of whom shall I be afraid?

segments.t: Dóminus protéctor vitæ meæ, * a quo trepidábo?

content.latin: 26:2 Dum apprópiant super me nocéntes, * ut edant carnes meas:
content.english: 26:2 Whilst the wicked draw near against me, * to eat my flesh.

segments.t: Dum apprópiant super me nocéntes, * ut edant carnes meas:

content.latin: 26:2 Qui tríbulant me inimíci mei, * ipsi infirmáti sunt, et cecidérunt.
content.english: 26:2 My enemies that trouble me, * have themselves been weakened, and have fallen.

segments.t: Qui tríbulant me inimíci mei, * ipsi infirmáti sunt, et cecidérunt.

content.latin: 26:3 Si consístant advérsum me castra, * non timébit cor meum.
content.english: 26:3 If armies in camp should stand together against me, * my heart shall not fear.

segments.t: Si consístant advérsum me castra, * non timébit cor meum.

content.latin: 26:3 Si exsúrgat advérsum me prǽlium, * in hoc ego sperábo.
content.english: 26:3 If a battle should rise up against me, * in this will I be confident.

segments.t: Si exsúrgat advérsum me prǽlium, * in hoc ego sperábo.

content.latin: 26:4 Unam pétii a Dómino, hanc requíram, * ut inhábitem in domo Dómini ómnibus diébus vitæ meæ:
content.english: 26:4 One thing I have asked of the Lord, this will I seek after; * that I may dwell in the house of the Lord all the days of my life.

segments.t: Unam pétii a Dómino, hanc requíram, * ut inhábitem in domo Dómini ómnibus diébus vitæ meæ:

content.latin: 26:4 Ut vídeam voluptátem Dómini, * et vísitem templum eius.
content.english: 26:4 That I may see the delight of the Lord, * and may visit his temple.

segments.t: Ut vídeam voluptátem Dómini, * et vísitem templum eius.

content.latin: 26:5 Quóniam abscóndit me in tabernáculo suo: * in die malórum protéxit me in abscóndito tabernáculi sui.
content.english: 26:5 For he hath hidden me in his tabernacle; * in the day of evils, he hath protected me in the secret place of his tabernacle.

segments.t: Quóniam abscóndit me in tabernáculo suo: * in die malórum protéxit me in abscóndito tabernáculi sui.

content.latin: 26:6 In petra exaltávit me: * et nunc exaltávit caput meum super inimícos meos.
content.english: 26:6 He hath exalted me upon a rock: * and now he hath lifted up my head above my enemies.

segments.t: In petra exaltávit me: * et nunc exaltávit caput meum super inimícos meos.

content.latin: 26:6 Circuívi, et immolávi in tabernáculo eius hóstiam vociferatiónis: * cantábo, et psalmum dicam Dómino.
content.english: 26:6 I have gone round, and have offered up in his tabernacle a sacrifice of jubilation: * I will sing, and recite a psalm to the Lord.

segments.t: Circuívi, et immolávi in tabernáculo eius hóstiam vociferatiónis: * cantábo, et psalmum dicam Dómino.

content.latin: 26:7 Exáudi, Dómine, vocem meam, qua clamávi ad te: * miserére mei, et exáudi me.
content.english: 26:7 Hear, O Lord, my voice, with which I have cried to thee: * have mercy on me and hear me.

segments.t: Exáudi, Dómine, vocem meam, qua clamávi ad te: * miserére mei, et exáudi me.

content.latin: 26:8 Tibi dixit cor meum, exquisívit te fácies mea: * fáciem tuam, Dómine, requíram.
content.english: 26:8 My heart hath said to thee: My face hath sought thee: * thy face, O Lord, will I still seek.

segments.t: Tibi dixit cor meum, exquisívit te fácies mea: * fáciem tuam, Dómine, requíram.

content.latin: 26:9 Ne avértas fáciem tuam a me: * ne declínes in ira a servo tuo.
content.english: 26:9 Turn not away thy face from me; * decline not in thy wrath from thy servant.

segments.t: Ne avértas fáciem tuam a me: * ne declínes in ira a servo tuo.

content.latin: 26:9 Adiútor meus esto: * ne derelínquas me, neque despícias me, Deus, salutáris meus.
content.english: 26:9 Be thou my helper, * forsake me not; do not thou despise me, O God my Saviour.

segments.t: Adiútor meus esto: * ne derelínquas me, neque despícias me, Deus, salutáris meus.

content.latin: 26:10 Quóniam pater meus, et mater mea dereliquérunt me: * Dóminus autem assúmpsit me.
content.english: 26:10 For my father and my mother have left me: * but the Lord hath taken me up.

segments.t: Quóniam pater meus, et mater mea dereliquérunt me: * Dóminus autem assúmpsit me.

content.latin: 26:11 Legem pone mihi, Dómine, in via tua: * et dírige me in sémitam rectam propter inimícos meos.
content.english: 26:11 Set me, O Lord, a law in thy way, * and guide me in the right path, because of my enemies.

segments.t: Legem pone mihi, Dómine, in via tua: * et dírige me in sémitam rectam propter inimícos meos.

content.latin: 26:12 Ne tradíderis me in ánimas tribulántium me: * quóniam insurrexérunt in me testes iníqui, et mentíta est iníquitas sibi.
content.english: 26:12 Deliver me not over to the will of them that trouble me; * for unjust witnesses have risen up against me; and iniquity hath lied to itself.

segments.t: Ne tradíderis me in ánimas tribulántium me: * quóniam insurrexérunt in me testes iníqui, et mentíta est iníquitas sibi.

content.latin: 26:13 Credo vidére bona Dómini * in terra vivéntium.
content.english: 26:13 I believe to see the good things of the Lord * in the land of the living.

segments.t: Credo vidére bona Dómini * in terra vivéntium.

content.latin: 26:14 Exspécta Dóminum, viríliter age: * et confortétur cor tuum, et sústine Dóminum.
content.english: 26:14 Expect the Lord, do manfully, * and let thy heart take courage, and wait thou for the Lord.

segments.t: Exspécta Dóminum, viríliter age: * et confortétur cor tuum, et sústine Dóminum.

content.latin: 27:1 Ad te, Dómine, clamábo, Deus meus, ne síleas a me: * nequándo táceas a me, et assimilábor descendéntibus in lacum.
content.english: 27:1 Unto thee will I cry, O Lord: my God, be not thou silent to me: * lest if thou be silent to me, I become like them that go down into the pit.

segments.t: Ad te, Dómine, clamábo, Deus meus, ne síleas a me: * nequándo táceas a me, et assimilábor descendéntibus in lacum.

content.latin: 27:2 Exáudi, Dómine, vocem deprecatiónis meæ dum oro ad te: * dum extóllo manus meas ad templum sanctum tuum.
content.english: 27:2 Hear, O Lord, the voice of my supplication, when I pray to thee; * when I lift up my hands to thy holy temple.

segments.t: Exáudi, Dómine, vocem deprecatiónis meæ dum oro ad te: * dum extóllo manus meas ad templum sanctum tuum.

content.latin: 27:3 Ne simul trahas me cum peccatóribus: * et cum operántibus iniquitátem ne perdas me.
content.english: 27:3 Draw me not away together with the wicked; * and with the workers of iniquity destroy me not:

segments.t: Ne simul trahas me cum peccatóribus: * et cum operántibus iniquitátem ne perdas me.

content.latin: 27:3 Qui loquúntur pacem cum próximo suo, * mala autem in córdibus eórum.
content.english: 27:3 Who speak peace with their neighbour, * but evils are in their hearts.

segments.t: Qui loquúntur pacem cum próximo suo, * mala autem in córdibus eórum.

content.latin: 27:4 Da illis secúndum ópera eórum, * et secúndum nequítiam adinventiónum ipsórum.
content.english: 27:4 Give them according to their works, * and according to the wickedness of their inventions.

segments.t: Da illis secúndum ópera eórum, * et secúndum nequítiam adinventiónum ipsórum.

content.english: 27:5 Because they have not understood the works of the Lord, and the operations of his hands: * thou shalt destroy them, and shalt not build them up.

content.latin: Deus, qui nobis per síngulos annos huius sancti templi tui consecratiónis réparas diem, et sacris semper mystériis repræséntas incólumes: exáudi preces pópuli tui, et præsta; ut quisquis hoc templum benefícia petitúrus ingréditur, cuncta se impetrásse lætétur.
content.english: O God, who dost every year bring round unto us again the day whereon this thine holy temple was hallowed, and bringest us again in soundness of body and mind to be present at thine holy worship, graciously hear the supplications of thy people, and grant that whosoever shall come into this thine house to ask good at thine hand, may be rejoiced in the obtaining of all his request.

content.latin: 30:2 In te, Dómine, sperávi, non confúndar in ætérnum: * in iustítia tua líbera me.
content.english: 30:2 In thee, O Lord, have I hoped, let me never be confounded: * deliver me in thy justice.

segments.t: In te, Dómine, sperávi, non confúndar in ætérnum: * in iustítia tua líbera me.

content.latin: 30:3 Inclína ad me aurem tuam, * accélera ut éruas me.
content.english: 30:3 Bow down thy ear to me: * make haste to deliver me.

segments.t: Inclína ad me aurem tuam, * accélera ut éruas me.

content.latin: 30:3 Esto mihi in Deum protectórem, et in domum refúgii: * ut salvum me fácias.
content.english: 30:3 Be thou unto me a God, a protector, and a house of refuge, * to save me.

segments.t: Esto mihi in Deum protectórem, et in domum refúgii: * ut salvum me fácias.

content.latin: 30:4 Quóniam fortitúdo mea, et refúgium meum es tu: * et propter nomen tuum dedúces me, et enútries me.
content.english: 30:4 For thou art my strength and my refuge; * and for thy name’s sake thou wilt lead me, and nourish me.

segments.t: Quóniam fortitúdo mea, et refúgium meum es tu: * et propter nomen tuum dedúces me, et enútries me.

content.latin: 30:5 Edúces me de láqueo hoc, quem abscondérunt mihi: * quóniam tu es protéctor meus.
content.english: 30:5 Thou wilt bring me out of this snare, which they have hidden for me: * for thou art my protector.

segments.t: Edúces me de láqueo hoc, quem abscondérunt mihi: * quóniam tu es protéctor meus.

content.latin: 30:6 In manus tuas comméndo spíritum meum: * redemísti me, Dómine, Deus veritátis.
content.english: 30:6 Into thy hands I commend my spirit: * thou hast redeemed me, O Lord, the God of truth.

segments.t: In manus tuas comméndo spíritum meum: * redemísti me, Dómine, Deus veritátis.

content.latin: 30:7 Odísti observántes vanitátes, * supervácue.
content.english: 30:7 Thou hast hated them that regard vanities, * to no purpose.

segments.t: Odísti observántes vanitátes, * supervácue.

content.latin: 30:7 Ego autem in Dómino sperávi: * exsultábo, et lætábor in misericórdia tua.
content.english: 30:7 But I have hoped in the Lord: * I will be glad and rejoice in thy mercy.

segments.t: Ego autem in Dómino sperávi: * exsultábo, et lætábor in misericórdia tua.

content.latin: 30:8 Quóniam respexísti humilitátem meam, * salvásti de necessitátibus ánimam meam.
content.english: 30:8 For thou hast regarded my humility, * thou hast saved my soul out of distresses.

segments.t: Quóniam respexísti humilitátem meam, * salvásti de necessitátibus ánimam meam.

content.latin: 30:9 Nec conclusísti me in mánibus inimíci: * statuísti in loco spatióso pedes meos.
content.english: 30:9 And thou hast not shut me up in the hands of the enemy: * thou hast set my feet in a spacious place.

segments.t: Nec conclusísti me in mánibus inimíci: * statuísti in loco spatióso pedes meos.

content.latin: 30:10 Miserére mei, Dómine, quóniam tríbulor: * conturbátus est in ira óculus meus, ánima mea, et venter meus:
content.english: 30:10 Have mercy on me, O Lord, for I am afflicted: * my eye is troubled with wrath, my soul, and my belly:

segments.t: Miserére mei, Dómine, quóniam tríbulor: * conturbátus est in ira óculus meus, ánima mea, et venter meus:

content.latin: 30:11 Quóniam defécit in dolóre vita mea: * et anni mei in gemítibus.
content.english: 30:11 For my life is wasted with grief: * and my years in sighs.

segments.t: Quóniam defécit in dolóre vita mea: * et anni mei in gemítibus.

content.latin: 30:11 Infirmáta est in paupertáte virtus mea: * et ossa mea conturbáta sunt.
content.english: 30:11 My strength is weakened through poverty * and my bones are disturbed.

segments.t: Infirmáta est in paupertáte virtus mea: * et ossa mea conturbáta sunt.

content.latin: 30:12 Super omnes inimícos meos factus sum oppróbrium et vicínis meis valde: * et timor notis meis.
content.english: 30:12 I am become a reproach among all my enemies, and very much to my neighbours; * and a fear to my acquaintance.

segments.t: Super omnes inimícos meos factus sum oppróbrium et vicínis meis valde: * et timor notis meis.

content.latin: 30:12 Qui vidébant me, foras fugérunt a me: * oblivióni datus sum, tamquam mórtuus a corde.
content.english: 30:12 They that saw me without fled from me. * I am forgotten as one dead from the heart.

segments.t: Qui vidébant me, foras fugérunt a me: * oblivióni datus sum, tamquam mórtuus a corde.

content.latin: 30:13 Factus sum tamquam vas pérditum: * quóniam audívi vituperatiónem multórum commorántium in circúitu.
content.english: 30:13 I am become as a vessel that is destroyed. * For I have heard the blame of many that dwell round about.

segments.t: Factus sum tamquam vas pérditum: * quóniam audívi vituperatiónem multórum commorántium in circúitu.

content.latin: 30:14 In eo dum convenírent simul advérsum me, * accípere ánimam meam consiliáti sunt.
content.english: 30:14 While they assembled together against me, * they consulted to take away my life.

segments.t: In eo dum convenírent simul advérsum me, * accípere ánimam meam consiliáti sunt.

content.latin: 30:15 Ego autem in te sperávi, Dómine: * dixi: Deus meus es tu: in mánibus tuis sortes meæ.
content.english: 30:15 But I have put my trust in thee, O Lord: * I said: Thou art my God. My lots are in thy hands.

segments.t: Ego autem in te sperávi, Dómine: * dixi: Deus meus es tu: in mánibus tuis sortes meæ.

content.latin: 30:16 Éripe me de manu inimicórum meórum, * et a persequéntibus me.
content.english: 30:16 Deliver me out of the hands of my enemies; * and from them that persecute me

segments.t: Éripe me de manu inimicórum meórum, * et a persequéntibus me.

content.latin: 30:17 Illústra fáciem tuam super servum tuum, salvum me fac in misericórdia tua: * Dómine, non confúndar, quóniam invocávi te.
content.english: 30:17 Make thy face to shine upon thy servant; save me in thy mercy. * Let me not be confounded, O Lord, for I have called upon thee.

segments.t: Illústra fáciem tuam super servum tuum, salvum me fac in misericórdia tua: * Dómine, non confúndar, quóniam invocávi te.

content.latin: 30:18 Erubéscant ímpii, et deducántur in inférnum: * muta fiant lábia dolósa.
content.english: 30:18 Let the wicked be ashamed, and be brought down to hell. * Let deceitful lips be made dumb.

segments.t: Erubéscant ímpii, et deducántur in inférnum: * muta fiant lábia dolósa.

content.latin: 30:19 Quæ loquúntur advérsus iustum iniquitátem: * in supérbia, et in abusióne.
content.english: 30:19 Which speak iniquity against the just, * with pride and abuse.

segments.t: Quæ loquúntur advérsus iustum iniquitátem: * in supérbia, et in abusióne.

content.english: 30:20 How great is the multitude of thy sweetness, O Lord, * which thou hast hidden for them that fear thee!

segments.t: Quam magna multitúdo dulcédinis tuæ, Dómine, * quam abscondísti timéntibus te.

content.latin: 30:20 Perfecísti eis, qui sperant in te, * in conspéctu filiórum hóminum.
content.english: 30:20 Which thou hast wrought for them that hope in thee, * in the sight of the sons of men.

segments.t: Perfecísti eis, qui sperant in te, * in conspéctu filiórum hóminum.

segments.t: Abscóndes eos in abscóndito faciéi tuæ * a conturbatióne hóminum.

content.latin: 30:21 Próteges eos in tabernáculo tuo * a contradictióne linguárum.
content.english: 30:21 Thou shalt protect them in thy tabernacle * from the contradiction of tongues.

segments.t: Próteges eos in tabernáculo tuo * a contradictióne linguárum.

content.english: 30:22 Blessed be the Lord, * for he hath shewn his wonderful mercy to me in a fortified city.

segments.t: Benedíctus Dóminus: * quóniam mirificávit misericórdiam suam mihi in civitáte muníta.

content.latin: 30:23 Ego autem dixi in excéssu mentis meæ: * Proiéctus sum a fácie oculórum tuórum.

segments.t: Ego autem dixi in excéssu mentis meæ: * Proiéctus sum a fácie oculórum tuórum.

segments.t: Ídeo exaudísti vocem oratiónis meæ, * dum clamárem ad te.

content.latin: 30:24 Dilígite Dóminum omnes sancti eius: * quóniam veritátem requíret Dóminus, et retríbuet abundánter faciéntibus supérbiam.
content.english: 30:24 O love the Lord, all ye his saints: * for the Lord will require truth, and will repay them abundantly that act proudly.

segments.t: Dilígite Dóminum omnes sancti eius: * quóniam veritátem requíret Dóminus, et retríbuet abundánter faciéntibus supérbiam.

content.latin: 30:25 Viríliter ágite, et confortétur cor vestrum, * omnes, qui sperátis in Dómino.
content.english: 30:25 Do ye manfully, and let your heart be strengthened, * all ye that hope in the Lord.

content.latin: Deus, qui nobis per síngulos annos huius sancti templi tui consecratiónis réparas diem, et sacris semper mystériis repræséntas incólumes: exáudi preces pópuli tui, et præsta; ut quisquis hoc templum benefícia petitúrus ingréditur, cuncta se impetrásse lætétur.
content.english: O God, who dost every year bring round unto us again the day whereon this thine holy temple was hallowed, and bringest us again in soundness of body and mind to be present at thine holy worship, graciously hear the supplications of thy people, and grant that whosoever shall come into this thine house to ask good at thine hand, may be rejoiced in the obtaining of all his request.

content.latin: Per Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Through Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.

content.english: Who ever dost thyself unmoved abide,

content.english: Grant to life’s day a calm unclouded ending,

content.latin: Quo vita nusquam décidat,

content.english: Psalm 31 [1]

content.latin: 31:1 Beáti quorum remíssæ sunt iniquitátes: * et quorum tecta sunt peccáta.
content.english: 31:1 Blessed are those whose iniquities are forgiven * and whose sins are covered.

segments.t: Beáti quorum remíssæ sunt iniquitátes: * et quorum tecta sunt peccáta.

content.latin: 31:2 Beátus vir, cui non imputávit Dóminus peccátum, * nec est in spíritu eius dolus.
content.english: 31:2 Blessed is the man to whom the Lord hath not imputed sin, * and in whose spirit there is no guile.

segments.t: Beátus vir, cui non imputávit Dóminus peccátum, * nec est in spíritu eius dolus.

content.latin: 31:3 Quóniam tácui, inveteravérunt ossa mea, * dum clamárem tota die.
content.english: 31:3 Because I was silent my bones grew old; * whilst I cried out all the day long.

segments.t: Quóniam tácui, inveteravérunt ossa mea, * dum clamárem tota die.

content.latin: 31:4 Quóniam die ac nocte graváta est super me manus tua: * convérsus sum in ærúmna mea, dum confígitur spina.
content.english: 31:4 For day and night thy hand was heavy upon me: * I am turned in my anguish, whilst the thorn is fastened.

segments.t: Quóniam die ac nocte graváta est super me manus tua: * convérsus sum in ærúmna mea, dum confígitur spina.

content.latin: 31:5 Delíctum meum cógnitum tibi feci: * et iniustítiam meam non abscóndi.
content.english: 31:5 I have acknowledged my sin to thee, * and my injustice I have not concealed.

segments.t: Delíctum meum cógnitum tibi feci: * et iniustítiam meam non abscóndi.

content.latin: 31:5 Dixi: Confitébor advérsum me iniustítiam meam Dómino: * et tu remisísti impietátem peccáti mei.
content.english: 31:5 I said I will confess against myself my injustice to the Lord: * and thou hast forgiven the wickedness of my sin.

segments.t: Dixi: Confitébor advérsum me iniustítiam meam Dómino: * et tu remisísti impietátem peccáti mei.

content.latin: 31:6 Pro hac orábit ad te omnis sanctus, * in témpore opportúno.
content.english: 31:6 For this shall every one that is holy pray to thee * in a seasonable time.

segments.t: Pro hac orábit ad te omnis sanctus, * in témpore opportúno.

content.latin: 31:6 Verúmtamen in dilúvio aquárum multárum, * ad eum non approximábunt.
content.english: 31:6 And yet in a flood of many waters, * they shall not come nigh unto him.

segments.t: Verúmtamen in dilúvio aquárum multárum, * ad eum non approximábunt.

content.latin: 31:7 Tu es refúgium meum a tribulatióne, quæ circúmdedit me: * exsultátio mea, érue me a circumdántibus me.
content.english: 31:7 Thou art my refuge from the trouble which hath encompassed me: * my joy, deliver me from them that surround me.

segments.t: Tu es refúgium meum a tribulatióne, quæ circúmdedit me: * exsultátio mea, érue me a circumdántibus me.

content.latin: 31:8 Intelléctum tibi dabo, et ínstruam te in via hac, qua gradiéris: * firmábo super te óculos meos.
content.english: 31:8 I will give thee understanding, and I will instruct thee in this way, in which thou shalt go: * I will fix my eyes upon thee.

segments.t: Intelléctum tibi dabo, et ínstruam te in via hac, qua gradiéris: * firmábo super te óculos meos.

content.latin: 31:9 Nolíte fíeri sicut equus et mulus, * quibus non est intelléctus.
content.english: 31:9 Do not become like the horse and the mule, * who have no understanding.

segments.t: Nolíte fíeri sicut equus et mulus, * quibus non est intelléctus.

content.latin: 31:9 In camo et freno maxíllas eórum constrínge, * qui non appróximant ad te.
content.english: 31:9 With bit and bridle bind fast their jaws, * who come not near unto thee.

segments.t: In camo et freno maxíllas eórum constrínge, * qui non appróximant ad te.

content.latin: 31:10 Multa flagélla peccatóris, * sperántem autem in Dómino misericórdia circúmdabit.
content.english: 31:10 Many are the scourges of the sinner, * but mercy shall encompass him that hopeth in the Lord.

segments.t: Multa flagélla peccatóris, * sperántem autem in Dómino misericórdia circúmdabit.

content.latin: 31:11 Lætámini in Dómino et exsultáte, iusti, * et gloriámini, omnes recti corde.
content.english: 31:11 Be glad in the Lord, and rejoice, ye just, * and glory, all ye right of heart.

segments.t: Lætámini in Dómino et exsultáte, iusti, * et gloriámini, omnes recti corde.

Psalmus 32(1-11)

content.latin: 32:1 Exsultáte, iusti, in Dómino: * rectos decet collaudátio.
content.english: 32:1 Rejoice in the Lord, O ye just: * praise becometh the upright.

segments.t: Exsultáte, iusti, in Dómino: * rectos decet collaudátio.

content.latin: 32:2 Confitémini Dómino in cíthara: * in psaltério decem chordárum psállite illi.
content.english: 32:2 Give praise to the Lord on the harp; * sing to him with the psaltery, the instrument of ten strings.

segments.t: Confitémini Dómino in cíthara: * in psaltério decem chordárum psállite illi.

content.latin: 32:3 Cantáte ei cánticum novum: * bene psállite ei in vociferatióne.
content.english: 32:3 Sing to him a new canticle, * sing well unto him with a loud noise.

segments.t: Cantáte ei cánticum novum: * bene psállite ei in vociferatióne.

content.latin: 32:4 Quia rectum est verbum Dómini, * et ómnia ópera eius in fide.
content.english: 32:4 For the word of the Lord is right, * and all his works are done with faithfulness.

segments.t: Quia rectum est verbum Dómini, * et ómnia ópera eius in fide.

content.latin: 32:5 Díligit misericórdiam et iudícium: * misericórdia Dómini plena est terra.
content.english: 32:5 He loveth mercy and judgment; * the earth is full of the mercy of the Lord.

segments.t: Díligit misericórdiam et iudícium: * misericórdia Dómini plena est terra.

content.latin: 32:6 Verbo Dómini cæli firmáti sunt: * et spíritu oris eius omnis virtus eórum.
content.english: 32:6 By the word of the Lord the heavens were established; * and all the power of them by the spirit of his mouth:

segments.t: Verbo Dómini cæli firmáti sunt: * et spíritu oris eius omnis virtus eórum.

content.latin: 32:7 Cóngregans sicut in utre aquas maris: * ponens in thesáuris abýssos.
content.english: 32:7 Gathering together the waters of the sea, as in a vessel; * laying up the depths in storehouses.

segments.t: Cóngregans sicut in utre aquas maris: * ponens in thesáuris abýssos.

content.latin: 32:8 Tímeat Dóminum omnis terra: * ab eo autem commoveántur omnes inhabitántes orbem.
content.english: 32:8 Let all the earth fear the Lord, * and let all the inhabitants of the world be in awe of him.

segments.t: Tímeat Dóminum omnis terra: * ab eo autem commoveántur omnes inhabitántes orbem.

content.latin: 32:9 Quóniam ipse dixit, et facta sunt: * ipse mandávit, et creáta sunt.
content.english: 32:9 For he spoke and they were made: * he commanded and they were created.

segments.t: Quóniam ipse dixit, et facta sunt: * ipse mandávit, et creáta sunt.

content.latin: 32:10 Dóminus díssipat consília géntium: * réprobat autem cogitatiónes populórum, et réprobat consília príncipum.
content.english: 32:10 The Lord bringeth to nought the counsels of nations; * and he rejecteth the devices of people, and casteth away the counsels of princes.

segments.t: Dóminus díssipat consília géntium: * réprobat autem cogitatiónes populórum, et réprobat consília príncipum.

content.latin: 32:11 Consílium autem Dómini in ætérnum manet: * cogitatiónes cordis eius in generatióne et generatiónem.
content.english: 32:11 But the counsel of the Lord standeth for ever: * the thoughts of his heart to all generations.

segments.t: Consílium autem Dómini in ætérnum manet: * cogitatiónes cordis eius in generatióne et generatiónem.

content.latin: 32:12 Beáta gens, cuius est Dóminus, Deus eius: * pópulus, quem elégit in hereditátem sibi.
content.english: 32:12 Blessed is the nation whose God is the Lord: * the people whom he hath chosen for his inheritance.

segments.t: Beáta gens, cuius est Dóminus, Deus eius: * pópulus, quem elégit in hereditátem sibi.

content.latin: 32:13 De cælo respéxit Dóminus: * vidit omnes fílios hóminum.
content.english: 32:13 The Lord hath looked from heaven: * he hath beheld all the sons of men.

segments.t: De cælo respéxit Dóminus: * vidit omnes fílios hóminum.

content.latin: 32:14 De præparáto habitáculo suo * respéxit super omnes, qui hábitant terram.
content.english: 32:14 From his habitation which he hath prepared, * he hath looked upon all that dwell on the earth.

segments.t: De præparáto habitáculo suo * respéxit super omnes, qui hábitant terram.

content.latin: 32:15 Qui finxit sigillátim corda eórum: * qui intéllegit ómnia ópera eórum.
content.english: 32:15 He who hath made the hearts of every one of them: * who understandeth all their works.

segments.t: Qui finxit sigillátim corda eórum: * qui intéllegit ómnia ópera eórum.

content.latin: 32:16 Non salvátur rex per multam virtútem: * et gigas non salvábitur in multitúdine virtútis suæ.
content.english: 32:16 The king is not saved by a great army: * nor shall the giant be saved by his own great strength.

segments.t: Non salvátur rex per multam virtútem: * et gigas non salvábitur in multitúdine virtútis suæ.

content.latin: 32:17 Fallax equus ad salútem: * in abundántia autem virtútis suæ non salvábitur.
content.english: 32:17 Vain is the horse for safety: * neither shall he be saved by the abundance of his strength.

segments.t: Fallax equus ad salútem: * in abundántia autem virtútis suæ non salvábitur.

content.latin: 32:18 Ecce, óculi Dómini super metuéntes eum: * et in eis, qui sperant super misericórdia eius:
content.english: 32:18 Behold the eyes of the Lord are on them that fear him: * and on them that hope in his mercy.

segments.t: Ecce, óculi Dómini super metuéntes eum: * et in eis, qui sperant super misericórdia eius:

content.latin: 32:19 Ut éruat a morte ánimas eórum: * et alat eos in fame.
content.english: 32:19 To deliver their souls from death; * and feed them in famine.

segments.t: Ut éruat a morte ánimas eórum: * et alat eos in fame.

content.latin: 32:20 Ánima nostra sústinet Dóminum: * quóniam adiútor et protéctor noster est.
content.english: 32:20 Our soul waiteth for the Lord: * for he is our helper and protector.

segments.t: Ánima nostra sústinet Dóminum: * quóniam adiútor et protéctor noster est.

content.latin: 32:21 Quia in eo lætábitur cor nostrum: * et in nómine sancto eius sperávimus.
content.english: 32:21 For in him our heart shall rejoice: * and in his holy name we have trusted.

segments.t: Quia in eo lætábitur cor nostrum: * et in nómine sancto eius sperávimus.

content.latin: 32:22 Fiat misericórdia tua, Dómine, super nos: * quemádmodum sperávimus in te.
content.english: 32:22 Let thy mercy, O Lord, be upon us, * as we have hoped in thee.

segments.t: Fiat misericórdia tua, Dómine, super nos: * quemádmodum sperávimus in te.

content.latin: Et abstérget Deus omnem lácrimam ab óculis eórum: et mors ultra non erit, neque luctus, neque clamor, neque dolor erit ultra, quia prima abiérunt. Et dixit qui sedébat in throno: Ecce nova fácio ómnia.
content.english: And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes, and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain; for the former things are passed away. And He That sat upon the throne said: Behold, I make all things new.

content.latin: Deus, qui nobis per síngulos annos huius sancti templi tui consecratiónis réparas diem, et sacris semper mystériis repræséntas incólumes: exáudi preces pópuli tui, et præsta; ut quisquis hoc templum benefícia petitúrus ingréditur, cuncta se impetrásse lætétur.
content.english: O God, who dost every year bring round unto us again the day whereon this thine holy temple was hallowed, and bringest us again in soundness of body and mind to be present at thine holy worship, graciously hear the supplications of thy people, and grant that whosoever shall come into this thine house to ask good at thine hand, may be rejoiced in the obtaining of all his request.

content.latin: Per Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Through Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
content.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

segments.t: Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.

content.latin: ℟. Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
content.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto thee.

segments.t: Et clamor meus ad te véniat.

content.latin: ℣. Benedicámus Dómino.
content.english: ℣. Let us bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedicámus Dómino.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.latin: ℣. Fidélium ánimæ per misericórdiam Dei requiéscant in pace.
content.english: ℣. May the souls of the faithful, through the mercy of God, rest in peace.

segments.t: Fidélium ánimæ per misericórdiam Dei requiéscant in pace.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Deus ✠ in adiutórium meum inténde.
content.english: ℣. O God, ✠ come to my assistance;

segments.t: Deus ✠ in adiutórium meum inténde.

content.latin: ℟. Dómine, ad adiuvándum me festína.
content.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me.

segments.t: Dómine, ad adiuvándum me festína.

content.latin: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: Allelúia.
content.english: Alleluia.

content.latin: Ant. Domum tuam, Dómine, * decet sanctitúdo in longitúdinem diérum.
content.english: Ant. Holiness becometh thine house, * O Lord, for ever.

segments.t: Ant.
Domum tuam, Dómine, * decet sanctitúdo in longitúdinem diérum.

content.latin: Psalmus 109 [1]
content.english: Psalm 109 [1]

segments.t: Psalmus 109

content.latin: 109:1 Dixit Dóminus Dómino meo: * Sede a dextris meis:
content.english: 109:1 The Lord said to my Lord: * Sit thou at my right hand:

segments.t: Dixit Dóminus Dómino meo: * Sede a dextris meis:

content.latin: 109:1 Donec ponam inimícos tuos, * scabéllum pedum tuórum.
content.english: 109:1 Until I make thy enemies * thy footstool.

segments.t: Donec ponam inimícos tuos, * scabéllum pedum tuórum.

content.latin: 109:2 Virgam virtútis tuæ emíttet Dóminus ex Sion: * domináre in médio inimicórum tuórum.
content.english: 109:2 The Lord will send forth the sceptre of thy power out of Sion: * rule thou in the midst of thy enemies.

segments.t: Virgam virtútis tuæ emíttet Dóminus ex Sion: * domináre in médio inimicórum tuórum.

content.latin: 109:3 Tecum princípium in die virtútis tuæ in splendóribus sanctórum: * ex útero ante lucíferum génui te.
content.english: 109:3 With thee is the principality in the day of thy strength: in the brightness of the saints: * from the womb before the day star I begot thee.

segments.t: Tecum princípium in die virtútis tuæ in splendóribus sanctórum: * ex útero ante lucíferum génui te.

content.latin: 109:4 Iurávit Dóminus, et non pœnitébit eum: * Tu es sacérdos in ætérnum secúndum órdinem Melchísedech.
content.english: 109:4 The Lord hath sworn, and he will not repent: * Thou art a priest for ever according to the order of Melchisedech.

segments.t: Iurávit Dóminus, et non pœnitébit eum: * Tu es sacérdos in ætérnum secúndum órdinem Melchísedech.

content.latin: 109:5 Dóminus a dextris tuis, * confrégit in die iræ suæ reges.
content.english: 109:5 The Lord at thy right hand * hath broken kings in the day of his wrath.

segments.t: Dóminus a dextris tuis, * confrégit in die iræ suæ reges.

content.latin: 109:6 Iudicábit in natiónibus, implébit ruínas: * conquassábit cápita in terra multórum.
content.english: 109:6 He shall judge among nations, he shall fill ruins: * he shall crush the heads in the land of many.

segments.t: Iudicábit in natiónibus, implébit ruínas: * conquassábit cápita in terra multórum.

content.latin: 109:7 De torrénte in via bibet: * proptérea exaltábit caput.
content.english: 109:7 He shall drink of the torrent in the way: * therefore shall he lift up the head.

segments.t: De torrénte in via bibet: * proptérea exaltábit caput.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.english: Ant. Holiness becometh thine house, O Lord, for ever.

content.latin: Psalmus 110 [2]
content.english: Psalm 110 [2]

segments.t: Psalmus 110

content.latin: 110:1 Confitébor tibi, Dómine, in toto corde meo: * in consílio iustórum, et congregatióne.
content.english: 110:1 I will praise thee, O Lord, with my whole heart; * in the council of the just, and in the congregation.

segments.t: Confitébor tibi, Dómine, in toto corde meo: * in consílio iustórum, et congregatióne.

content.latin: 110:2 Magna ópera Dómini: * exquisíta in omnes voluntátes eius.
content.english: 110:2 Great are the works of the Lord: * sought out according to all his wills.

segments.t: Magna ópera Dómini: * exquisíta in omnes voluntátes eius.

content.latin: 110:3 Conféssio et magnificéntia opus eius: * et iustítia eius manet in sǽculum sǽculi.
content.english: 110:3 His work is praise and magnificence: * and his justice continueth for ever and ever.

segments.t: Conféssio et magnificéntia opus eius: * et iustítia eius manet in sǽculum sǽculi.

content.latin: 110:4 Memóriam fecit mirabílium suórum, miséricors et miserátor Dóminus: * escam dedit timéntibus se.
content.english: 110:4 He hath made a remembrance of his wonderful works, being a merciful and gracious Lord: * he hath given food to them that fear him.

segments.t: Memóriam fecit mirabílium suórum, miséricors et miserátor Dóminus: * escam dedit timéntibus se.

content.latin: 110:5 Memor erit in sǽculum testaménti sui: * virtútem óperum suórum annuntiábit pópulo suo:
content.english: 110:5 He will be mindful for ever of his covenant: * he will shew forth to his people the power of his works.

segments.t: Memor erit in sǽculum testaménti sui: * virtútem óperum suórum annuntiábit pópulo suo:

content.latin: 110:7 Ut det illis hereditátem géntium: * ópera mánuum eius véritas, et iudícium.
content.english: 110:7 That he may give them the inheritance of the Gentiles: * the works of his hands are truth and judgment.

segments.t: Ut det illis hereditátem géntium: * ópera mánuum eius véritas, et iudícium.

content.latin: 110:8 Fidélia ómnia mandáta eius: confirmáta in sǽculum sǽculi, * facta in veritáte et æquitáte.
content.english: 110:8 All his commandments are faithful: confirmed for ever and ever, * made in truth and equity.

segments.t: Fidélia ómnia mandáta eius: confirmáta in sǽculum sǽculi, * facta in veritáte et æquitáte.

content.latin: 110:9 Redemptiónem misit pópulo suo: * mandávit in ætérnum testaméntum suum.
content.english: 110:9 He hath sent redemption to his people: * he hath commanded his covenant for ever.

segments.t: Redemptiónem misit pópulo suo: * mandávit in ætérnum testaméntum suum.

content.latin: 110:9 (fit reverentia) Sanctum, et terríbile nomen eius: * inítium sapiéntiæ timor Dómini.
content.english: 110:9 (bow head) Holy and terrible is his name: * the fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom.

segments.t: 110:9 (fit reverentia)
Sanctum, et terríbile nomen eius: * inítium sapiéntiæ timor Dómini.

content.latin: 110:10 Intelléctus bonus ómnibus faciéntibus eum: * laudátio eius manet in sǽculum sǽculi.
content.english: 110:10 A good understanding to all that do it: * his praise continueth for ever and ever.

segments.t: Intelléctus bonus ómnibus faciéntibus eum: * laudátio eius manet in sǽculum sǽculi.

content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.english: Ant. My house shall be called the house of prayer.

content.latin: Ant. Hæc est domus Dómini * fírmiter ædificáta, bene fundáta est supra firmam petram.
content.english: Ant. This is the Lord's house * stoutly builded, well founded upon a sure rock.

segments.t: Ant.
Hæc est domus Dómini * fírmiter ædificáta, bene fundáta est supra firmam petram.

content.latin: Psalmus 111 [3]
content.english: Psalm 111 [3]

segments.t: Psalmus 111

content.latin: 111:1 Beátus vir, qui timet Dóminum: * in mandátis eius volet nimis.
content.english: 111:1 Blessed is the man that feareth the Lord: * he shall delight exceedingly in his commandments.

segments.t: Beátus vir, qui timet Dóminum: * in mandátis eius volet nimis.

content.latin: 111:2 Potens in terra erit semen eius: * generátio rectórum benedicétur.
content.english: 111:2 His seed shall be mighty upon earth: * the generation of the righteous shall be blessed.

segments.t: Potens in terra erit semen eius: * generátio rectórum benedicétur.

content.latin: 111:3 Glória, et divítiæ in domo eius: * et iustítia eius manet in sǽculum sǽculi.
content.english: 111:3 Glory and wealth shall be in his house: * and his justice remaineth for ever and ever.

segments.t: Glória, et divítiæ in domo eius: * et iustítia eius manet in sǽculum sǽculi.

content.latin: 111:4 Exórtum est in ténebris lumen rectis: * miséricors, et miserátor, et iustus.
content.english: 111:4 To the righteous a light is risen up in darkness: * he is merciful, and compassionate and just.

segments.t: Exórtum est in ténebris lumen rectis: * miséricors, et miserátor, et iustus.

content.latin: 111:5 Iucúndus homo qui miserétur et cómmodat, dispónet sermónes suos in iudício: * quia in ætérnum non commovébitur.
content.english: 111:5 Acceptable is the man that sheweth mercy and lendeth: he shall order his words with judgment: * because he shall not be moved for ever.

segments.t: Iucúndus homo qui miserétur et cómmodat, dispónet sermónes suos in iudício: * quia in ætérnum non commovébitur.

content.latin: 111:7 In memória ætérna erit iustus: * ab auditióne mala non timébit.
content.english: 111:7 The just shall be in everlasting remembrance: * he shall not fear the evil hearing.

segments.t: In memória ætérna erit iustus: * ab auditióne mala non timébit.

content.latin: 111:7 Parátum cor eius speráre in Dómino, confirmátum est cor eius: * non commovébitur donec despíciat inimícos suos.
content.english: 111:7 His heart is ready to hope in the Lord: his heart is strengthened, * he shall not be moved until he look over his enemies.

segments.t: Parátum cor eius speráre in Dómino, confirmátum est cor eius: * non commovébitur donec despíciat inimícos suos.

content.latin: 111:9 Dispérsit, dedit paupéribus: iustítia eius manet in sǽculum sǽculi, * cornu eius exaltábitur in glória.
content.english: 111:9 He hath distributed, he hath given to the poor: his justice remaineth for ever and ever: * his horn shall be exalted in glory.

segments.t: Dispérsit, dedit paupéribus: iustítia eius manet in sǽculum sǽculi, * cornu eius exaltábitur in glória.

content.latin: 111:10 Peccátor vidébit, et irascétur, déntibus suis fremet et tabéscet: * desidérium peccatórum períbit.
content.english: 111:10 The wicked shall see, and shall be angry, he shall gnash with his teeth and pine away: * the desire of the wicked shall perish.

segments.t: Peccátor vidébit, et irascétur, déntibus suis fremet et tabéscet: * desidérium peccatórum períbit.

Hæc est domus Dómini fírmiter ædificáta, bene fundáta est supra firmam petram.
